title: Descent to finite coefficient fields
statement: Let k be a field, Λ an Artinian local k-algebra with residue field K, σ:K→Λ a section of reduction, t a finite set with ideal span m_Λ, and c a finite subset of K such that i(k) lies in the subring generated by t∪σ(k(c)). Then there is a finite c0⊂K containing c such that, for every finite s⊃c0, C_s of [def-weil-pbc-artinian-coefficient-subalgebra] is an Artinian local ring, its inclusion C_s→Λ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], its maximal ideal extends to m_Λ, and it is essentially of finite type over k [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 07FG, proof, final presentation, flatness and essential finite type paragraphs (parent steps 8–11)

proof.text: Apply eventual flatness to obtain d and set c0=c union d. For s containing c0, monotonicity of intermediate-field adjoin and ring closure carries the coefficient containment from c to s.

Apply the coefficient-subalgebra structure lemma with t contained in m by the span hypothesis. It gives locality, Artinianness, contraction of m and the residue k-algebra equivalence with k(s). The contraction identity implies the extended maximal ideal is contained in m. Conversely every generator t belongs to C_s and to its maximal ideal, so the extension contains span(t)=m. Thus equality holds.

The field k(s) is essentially of finite type by IntermediateField.fg_adjoin_finset and IntermediateField.essFiniteType_iff. Transport this property to the residue field through the supplied k-algebra equivalence. Apply the Artinian local residue criterion to the structure map k→C_s. Combine this with the flatness clause and the maximal-ideal equality.
